title: Test design: Count Pairs
summary: How many pairs of positions add up to a target, each pair counted once.
spec:
`countPairs(nums, target)` returns how many pairs of **positions** `i < j` have `nums[i] + nums[j] == target`. For `[1, 5, 2, 4]` and a target of `6` that's `2` (1 + 5 and 2 + 4).

Each pair of positions counts once, whichever order you read it in. Equal values at different positions are different positions: `[2, 2, 2]` with a target of `4` has `3` pairs. A value never pairs with itself. Fewer than two values give `0`.

variants.title: Lets a value pair with itself
variants.defect: The inner loop starts at i instead of i + 1, so a value equal to half the target is counted as a pair with itself.
variants.gap: In your cases, no value is exactly half the target. What happens when one is?

variants.title: Stops at the first pair it finds
variants.defect: It returns 1 as soon as one pair adds up, so it answers whether a pair exists, never how many there are.
variants.gap: Every case of yours has at most one pair. Try an array where two different pairs add up to the target.

variants.title: Remembers which values it has seen, not how many times
variants.defect: It keeps a set of the values seen so far, so with repeated values it misses pairs: [2, 2, 2] with a target of 4 has 3 pairs and it finds 2.
variants.gap: Your values are all different. Repeated values make more pairs than a set of values can count.

variants.title: Never pairs anything with the last value
variants.defect: The inner loop runs j < nums.length - 1, so a pair that uses the last value is never counted.
variants.gap: In your cases, the pairs that add up are never at the end of the array. Put one there.
